Lemma 8.1(i)-(ii) are proved for actual dyadic local-field structures on the selected finite completions: the continuous finite-dimensional extension is constructed, order scaling holds for every nonzero completed-base-field element, relative quadratic-defect scaling is proved from mapped square approximations, and the completion order, defect, and ramification normalizations are identified with the BONG notions. The exact He--Hu adjacent and two-step coefficient criterion is preserved, and every actual lower good BONG has an actual upper integral-lattice good-BONG realization with precisely the mapped values. This is the strongest conclusion supported by the written proof of Lemma 8.1(iii); the literal identification with the preassigned localized scalar-extension lattice L_P remains open because the cited He--Hu Lemma 2.2 concludes only for some lattice. Proposition 8.2, the global deduction in Theorem 1.5, and Theorem 1.9 are proved conditionally from explicit number-field arithmetic proof-data packages; Proposition 8.2 is derived from positive-definite globalization, localization of integrality and representation, and local-equivalence transport rather than assumed as a final field; Theorem 1.9's finite-place conclusion is derived from separate non-dyadic, dyadic unary, and dyadic higher-rank laws, and its local-to-global step is derived target-by-target from rank and integrality localization plus an explicit strong-approximation representation law; the number-field discriminant/ramification equivalence, both directed uses, the ramified dyadic-prime witness, and positivity are proved; canonical number-field global data defines the dyadic predicate, ramification index, and discriminant proposition from the standard height-one spectrum and derives all arithmetic compatibility fields from a place equivalence; Lemma 8.3, Theorem 1.7, and Theorem 1.8 have only n >= 2 even source-facing endpoints, while Theorem 1.7's rank-independent final contradiction is separately proved from an explicit local-defect premise; no unrestricted odd endpoint is exported; reports 23 and 27-42

reviewNotice: The semantic basis is the author-corrected v5 TeX manuscript identified by filename and SHA-256; it is not redistributed in the Review Kit. Theorem 1.1 has a checked proof, not merely a proposition encoding. The complete n >= 1 local-field implication underlying Theorem 1.5 is proved, including its unary branch. Lemma 8.1(i)-(ii) are proved on actual dyadic completions, and their completion-side order, defect, and ramification invariants are identified with the BONG normalization. Every actual lower good BONG has an actual upper integral-lattice good-BONG realization with precisely the mapped values. This is the strongest conclusion supported by the written proof of part (iii), but it does not identify that realization with the preassigned localized scalar-extension lattice L_P: the cited He--Hu Lemma 2.2 only produces some lattice, and v5 supplies no carrier-identification argument. The global deduction in Theorem 1.5, Proposition 8.2, and Theorem 1.9 have conditional proof endpoints over explicit arithmetic proof-data packages; Proposition 8.2 is derived from lower positive-definite globalization, localization, and equivalence-transport laws rather than assumed as a final field, and Theorem 1.9's finite-place conclusion is derived from its three source branches while its local-to-global step is derived from target-wise localization plus a separate strong-approximation representation law. The number-field discriminant/ramification equivalence, both directed uses, the ramified dyadic-prime witness, and positivity are proved. Canonical number-field global data defines the dyadic predicate, ramification index, and discriminant proposition directly from a supplied equivalence with the standard height-one spectrum; all former arithmetic compatibility statements, primality, coverage, and Section 8 discriminant fields are then derived. The place equivalence and the concrete number-field global-lattice/localization, local sum-of-squares, and strong-approximation instances remain excluded. The unrestricted odd statement of v5 Corollary 6.3 is false: a kernel-checked e=2, n=3 counterexample proves nonisometry to the diagonal lattice with the same six coefficients. Lemma 8.3, Theorem 1.7, and Theorem 1.8 are therefore exported only for n >= 2 even. For Theorem 1.7 the rank-independent final contradiction is additionally proved from an explicit local-defect premise, but the uncited odd coefficient calculation is not encoded as a law and no unrestricted odd endpoint remains. The author-corrected v5 Lemma 7.1 is formalized, and the literal even- and odd-rank families both satisfy the testing equivalence and row-by-row deletion minimality required by Theorem 1.3. The obsolete broader publisher Lemma 7.1(ii) remains refuted for e > 1 and is retained only as a comparison-source regression check. Every literal table model is proved classic-maximal, but no theorem classifies all classic-maximal lattices by those rows. Report 35 records an exact source-only local Review Kit pass for commit c1ee018, including all payload hashes, six Classic audits, the enforcing axiom gate, and exact clean dependency pins; it is historical rather than evidence for the newer Reports 36 and 38--42 code and is not GitHub CI or release evidence. Grade D records both the false authoritative-v5 Corollary 6.3 odd statement and the Lemma 8.1(iii) carrier gap, as well as incomplete whole-paper coverage; concrete global instances, current-code clean-kit verification, GitHub release verification, and human semantic sign-off remain outside the present completion claim.
